author: The Daily Reflector
title: ECU softball: Gall, No. 22 Stanford too much for Pirates - NewsBreak
text:
By The Daily Reflector ,
12 hours ago
An early home run Wednesday gave East Carolina's nationally-ranked softball opponent the momentum it needed to breeze through the finish line.
No. 22 Stanford benefited from Ava Gall's deep fly in the second inning and eventually handed ECU a 7-2 loss at Max R. Joyner Family Stadium.
Gall ended with two hits and a game-best four RBIs for the Cardinal (19-8). Her three-run jack barely got past the glove of Pirates (22-12) center fielder Kanisha Anderson and cued a 3-0 advantage.
ECU got on the board in the third when Anna Sawyer hit a sacrifice fly in foul territory to make it 4-1.
The visitors brought across a couple more in the fourth to pull ahead 6-1. Another Pirates run came home during a productive sixth inning. But the deficit stood at 6-2 when Hailey Deter grounded into a double play with the bases loaded.
Gall gave Stanford its final score on a RBI fielder's choice in the seventh.
Trinity Nichols led the Pirates offense, finishing 2-for-3. Sydney Rainford was tagged with the loss after allowing four earned through 2.2 innings to start.
ECU returns to American Conference play Friday, hosting UAB at 5 p.m. to start a three-game series.
Women's golf places 4th
The Pirates women's golf team shot a tournament score of 908 to finish fourth Tuesday at the City of Oaks Collegiate in Raleigh.
Junior Ella Stalvey paced ECU, finishing tied for fifth after carding a three-round score of 222 (6-over). It marked her first career top-five finish.
Fellow classmate Nicole Nash claimed a share of 12th place with an 11-over par 227, while graduate senior Marta Perez finished tied for 14th after her score of 228. Danielle Modder posted a 233 and Lisa Forss rounded out the Pirates starters by carding a 242.
Host, and No. 44 ranked NC State, won the team title with a total of 888 (24-over), finishing 13 shots ahead of Rutgers (901).
Behar earns weekly honors
ECU lacrosse's Jaime Behar has been named the American Conference's Goalkeeper of the Week, the league announced Monday.
The senior made 12 saves and allowed just six goals in an 8-7 win over Temple last Saturday. Behar's save with 38 seconds remaining sealed the victory.
ECU is back in action Saturday, traveling to No. 1 North Carolina at noon.
